info.title: Readable instructions
info.text:
Pseudocode focuses on the algorithm.

Use consistent, unambiguous notation.

OCR exam reference language is one defined notation.

Challenge: Why must pseudocode still be precise?

Another person must be able to follow it and obtain the intended result.

info.title: Assignment or equality
info.text:
Assignment changes a stored value.

A comparison checks a relationship.

In OCR notation, = assigns and == compares.

Challenge: Explain the different jobs of = and == here.

= assigns a value. == compares two values and produces true or false.

info.title: Write selection
info.text:
Put the true actions inside the IF branch.

Use ELSE for the alternative.

End the selection clearly.

Challenge: What output is produced for age 12?

Allowed, because 12 >= 12 is true.

info.title: Write repetition
info.text:
Use a count-controlled loop for a fixed count.

Initialise a running total once.

Put repeated input and addition in the loop.

Challenge: Why is print(total) after the loop?

The required result is the final total after all three inputs have been added.

info.title: Translate to Python
info.text:
Keep the same inputs, branches and outputs.

Python uses a colon and indentation.

Python range excludes its stop value.

Challenge: Why is the stop value 4 rather than 3?

Python range(1, 4) includes 1, 2 and 3 but excludes 4.

info.title: Check equivalence
info.text:
Different representations can do the same job.

Use identical inputs to compare outputs.

Check loop counts and boundary conditions.

Challenge: Why can a direct copy of loop bounds be wrong?

OCR for loops include the end value while Python range excludes the stop value.
